summary: @servicetitan/microfront-auth preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes bundled obfuscated payload
details: package.json sets scripts.preinstall to 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime v1.3.13 from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it via execFileSync to run the sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a ~727 KB single-line file tagged '// @bun @bun-cjs' with obfuscator.io fingerprints (large shuffled string array, hex-named identifiers, encoded literal-lookup routine); it is not valid Node input and its behavior is only observable under Bun. This is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern: an official runtime is fetched from its own project host, but the fetched runtime is then used to execute obfuscated bundled code whose contents cannot be reviewed by Node-based tooling, running with the installer's privileges on npm install. The package is published under the @servicetitan scope with empty description, no README, and a repository URL pointing at github.com/servicetitan/playground.git — metadata consistent with impersonation of internal ServiceTitan tooling rather than a real published library.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
